Team — attaching a draft answer set and our BYOK integration guide for review (redwood_byok_integration_guide.pdf). Highlights: 

- Key storage model: Redwood uses envelope encryption. Customer plaintext key material is never stored in Redwood in plaintext. When customers provide keys via BYOK, keys are imported into a KMS/HSM and then used to wrap per-customer data encryption keys (DEKs).
- HSM support: We support integrations with cloud HSMs (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM-backed keys) and partner-managed on-prem HSMs via PKCS#11. For private deployments we can configure PKCS#11-based key stores to talk to customer HSMs.
- BYOK import options: 1) Customer supplies wrapped key material for import into our managed KMS; 2) Customer provides HSM-controlled signing/import endpoints (PKCS#11) for direct provisioning.
- Rotation: We offer automated DEK rotation on configurable cadences (default 90 days). CMKs (customer master keys) are rotated per customer policy; if the customer controls the CMK, rotation is customer-managed via their KMS. Emergency revocation workflows exist and are tied to our incident runbook.
- TLS: We require TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites (TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 or equivalent). mTLS is supported for private and dedicated endpoints; mutual certs are optional but recommended for high-trust integrations.

Please review the attached draft answers in the workbook before I send to Stratagem. Also attached: hsm_reference_diagram.pdf (high-level).

Naomi Feldman

Elena / Jose — attaching the completed workbook (questionnaire_filled.xlsx) and an HSM reference diagram (hsm_reference_diagram.pdf). Key points up front:

- No plaintext persisted by Redwood: Customer master key material is either imported as wrapped key material or remains under customer control in their HSM. We never persist plaintext CMKs.
- HSM options: We support cloud HSMs (AWS/Azure) and on-prem HSMs via PKCS#11 connectors for Private deployments. For Dedicated/Hosted we can integrate with partner HSM providers; customers can also bring their own HSM.
- BYOK workflows: 1) Import wrapped keys via secure import APIs (you retain the unwrapped key during the import flow), or 2) Use PKCS#11-backed provisioning where the key never leaves your HSM.
- Rotation and TTLs: Default automated DEK rotation is 90 days; configurable from 30–180 days. CMK rotation is handled according to the customer's KMS policy.
- TLS: We enforce TLS1.2+ on all endpoints. For highest assurance, enable mTLS for ingestion and management endpoints. We enforce strong ciphers and perfect forward secrecy.

Also including a DocuSign link for the BYOK addendum in case you'd like legal to review: https://www.docusign.com/secure/Stratagem-BYOK-Addendum

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the diagram and the import flow.

Elena — thanks for the follow-ups. Answers below and attaching a short audit log sample (audit_log_sample.txt) and our SOC2 summary link.

1) Plaintext CMK access: Confirmed — Redwood does not store or access customer CMKs in plaintext. Import flows are either: a) secure import of wrapped key material where the customer unwraps locally and provides wrapped bytes for import; or b) PKCS#11-backed provisioning where the CMK never leaves the customer's HSM. In both flows we only operate on wrapped material or wrapped DEKs.

2) PKCS#11 connector hosting: For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments we configure the PKCS#11 connector to run inside the customer's network/HSM enclave; the connector can be deployed as a lightweight agent/container and talks directly to your HSM. For Redwood Hosted/Dedicated customers we can offer a managed connector hosted in a partner environment with strict network controls, but for high-assurance customers we recommend running the connector inside your network.

3) Audit log sample: attached (audit_log_sample.txt). The sample shows events for: key_import.request, key_import.complete, dek.rotate, cmk.rotate.request, and cmk.rotate.complete with actor IDs and timestamps. Production logs include request IDs and operator metadata; we can provide additional fields under NDA.

Rotation & emergency: Automated DEK rotation defaults to 90 days (configurable). Emergency revocation is supported: an admin can mark a CMK revoked which prevents new DEK wrapping; existing DEKs can be rewrapped under a new CMK per your process. We also maintain a playbook for incident-driven key rotation and forensic exports.

SOC2 and compliance: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1SOC2-Redwood-Summary — the SOC2 report and audit artifacts can be shared with execs under an NDA.

If you'd like, Naomi can schedule a short technical walkthrough next week to demo a PKCS#11 import flow and show the logging format.

Regards,
